headlines.title: The 5 most interesting analyst questions from Old Dominion Freight Line’s Q3 earnings call
headlines.summary: Old Dominion Freight Line's third quarter was shaped by margin expansion and higher revenue, yet the market responded negatively to the results. Management attributed the quarter’s performance to effective pricing discipline and operational leverage, as the company continued to see improvements in revenue per shipment and network efficiency.

headlines.title: Old Dominion: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

headlines.title: Old Dominion Freight Line (ODFL) Stock Price Retreats As Q3 Results Fuel Margin Debate
headlines.summary: Old Dominion Freight Line just posted Q3 2026 results that spotlight one thing above everything else: a powerful profit engine. Revenue reached US$1.59b while earnings per share came in at US$1.65, with the operating ratio improving to 71.5% as pricing and mix did the heavy lifting. Yet the stock dropped about 7% on the day.

description: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. operates as a less-than-truckload motor carrier in the United States and North America. The company offers regional, inter-regional, and national less-than-truckload services, as well as expedited transportation services. It also provides various value-added services, including container drayage, truckload brokerage, and supply chain consulting. In addition, the company operates fleet maintenance centers. As of December 31, 2025, it owned and operated 10,184 tractors, 30,824 linehaul trailers, and 14,313 pickup and delivery trailers. Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. was founded in 1934 and is headquartered in Thomasville, North Carolina.
